messages:
jordan: heads up — seeing a cluster of GPU attach holds in us-west1 starting ~06:10 UTC. probes show attach queue depth spiking and node-level iowait up.
anika: wow, got the alert. any correlation with janitor/cleaner runs? last scrub window was 06:00.
carlos: heap of prior incidents where deep scrubs + nightly batch jobs caused ephemeral NVMe iops collapse. maybe same.
sre-bot: Alert: gpu-attach-delay > 300s (us-west1) — affected pods: 42, nodes with high io_wait: 18.
jordan: pasting a filtered dmesg snippet from one affected host:
```
[06:12:03] nvme0: async queue full, read latency rising
[06:12:08] scrubber: compact loop paused, backpressure -> throttle
[06:12:15] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345
```
lina: that looks like scrub/compaction hogging the queue, causing tiny writes/read amplification. GPUs waiting on attaches until scratch volume mounts.
anika: can we disable deep-scrub cron for the next 2h in us-west1 only? quick mitigation.
carlos: downside: leaving scrub paused increases cold badblock window, but tradeoff might be acceptable for 2h to restore capacity. need to signal storage team.
jordan: agree. rolling change: stop scrub on a small canary subset first (10 nodes) then expand if metrics improve.
lina: +1. also propose temporary routing: divert new GPU provisioning to dedicated pool for latency-sensitive teams to avoid user impact.
anika: who owns the scrub job? @storage-runbooks or runbook on call?
sre-bot: storage-runbooks notified: incident refs 4788881234.
storage-runbooks: (automated) Received request to pause deep-scrub in cluster us-west1. Confirming owners.
carlos: if we pause scrubs, can we tighten fstrim cadence or increase write coalesce to reduce small write pressure in the short window?
jordan: good call — will flip fstrim to 30m instead of 4h on canary nodes. command used:
```
ssh node-abc && sudo systemctl stop deep-scrub && sudo crontab -l | sed '/deep-scrub/d' | crontab -
```
anika: metrics after 10m of canary stop: attach queue depth down 60%, attach success rate back to normal for canary nodes.
lina: nice. any sign of corruption? need to ensure we don't introduce silent data issues while pausing.
jordan: no new checksum errors observed in the 20m window. will keep rolling and monitor S.M.A.R.T and parity-check logs.
carlos: please include cost note: routing to dedicated pool increases ephemeral-GPU cost ~15% for the diverted workload for the 2h window. tag owners.
anika: tagging owners and sending a short status to #incidents. also adding a follow-up action: storage team to run a root-cause for why deep-scrub caused such disproportionate small-write amplification.
jordan: postmortem action items I'll track: 1) investigate cleaner backpressure algorithm, 2) add per-node scrub rate limit by GPU-slot pressure, 3) plan delayed-scrub window for heavy-provision regions.
lina: also add a monitoring alert for scrub-caused iowait spike so we catch this earlier and auto-throttle scrubs.
storage-runbooks: acknowledged. pausing scrubs in us-west1 canary nodes completed at 06:35 UTC. monitoring link: https://metrics.redwood/incident/4788881234
jordan: thanks all — expanding pause to next 40 nodes now. will update when region load stabilizes. :thumbsup:
